corpusSummary: This corpus chronicles a 2026 wave of social-science work using large language models to study real-world AI use, trust, and safety; to augment research methods; to transform education and literacy; and to illuminate societal, cultural, and governance implications—from misinformation and representation to public participation and policy-relevant applications. These themes surface across health, climate, work, and urban studies, highlighting both scalable opportunities and context-specific challenges.

themes.name: Trust, safety, and ethics in AI-enabled interactions and information
themes.description: A growing set of studies investigates how users perceive AI—humanness, empathy, and reliability—alongside safety, misinformation, bias, and governance implications across health, education, and everyday decision making.

themes.name: AI as a transformative research tool: methods, collaboration, and validation
themes.description: Researchers deploy LLMs and AI pipelines to code, analyze, simulate, summarize, and organize data, producing new workflows while emphasizing validation, transparency, and researcher authority.

themes.name: AI in education: adoption, pedagogy, assessment, and AI literacy
themes.description: Empirical work on how AI changes teaching, learning, assessment, and student skills, with attention to adoption barriers, teacher readiness, and AI-supported literacy across age groups.

themes.name: Societal, cultural, and governance dimensions of AI deployment
themes.description: Studies examine how AI reshapes social networks, representation, polarization, public participation, cultural practices, and policy, including equity, digital divide, and global south contexts.
